source_correspondence: The theorem explicitly retains the characteristic zero level, oriented strict endpoint signs, arbitrary real classical order and the full negation of every finite forcing threshold.

Elliptic order adjustment, compact homogeneous tube quantization and its full two-sided graph inverses reduce the actual operator. The limiting characteristic cone lies in the original one; complex multiplier invariance preserves nearby forbidden transitions.

Common-domain complex division removes temporal momentum from every lower homogeneous term. The classical series is realized using the actual construction in FCM:N2. A full-frequency cone cutoff and a separate off-diagonal transverse argument justify the tangential calculus.

Complex nonstationary estimates are uniform in Fourier frequency and packet scale. Rapid distribution pairings and quantitative proper-kernel Fourier estimates prove all operator and graph localization statements.
The upper negative Sobolev bound and the scaled-test lower bound retain every dimension factor and permit a degenerate time Hessian. The simple model also has a two-sided norm at every real order.
The exact simple Gaussian phase has the correct quartic imaginary correction. Full graph transfer yields a contradiction to the actual adjoint estimate at any nearby positive-bracket point.
The finite complex phase equations explicitly solve for both real center derivatives and every coupled phase coefficient. No holomorphic extension of the smooth symbol is assumed.

Flatness gives one extended compact existence interval. Uniform center Jacobian control proves a genuine diffeomorphism. The sign-transfer lemma forces an interior imaginary minimum with positive transverse Hessian and nonzero real critical covectors.

The symbol-action proof uses uniform Schwartz rescaling and Fourier moments, retaining the cancellation of dimensional factors. All output and parameter derivatives, arbitrary symbol orders and separated frequency tails are controlled.

Every product-rule power is accounted for. Finite coupled linear ODEs determine the complete amplitude jets, including scalar Hessian and lower-symbol terms, on the same interval. Cutoffs meet only strictly positive imaginary phase.

Explicit finite phase, amplitude and symbol depths make all four differentiated error exponents smaller than the required residual power. The actual Sobolev contradiction and full base-neighborhood consequence follow.

Three solved exercises supply exact moving-center signs, the complete quadratic transport correction and an infinitely flat exact adjoint model. Twenty-five symbolic checks support the finite identities; they do not replace analytic proofs.

Theorem 26.4.7 and its reduced form, Corollary 26.4.8 and Lemmas 26.4.14–16 have receiving proofs. Together with the previous solvability and geometry lessons, Section 26.4 receiving content is complete.
